Chapter 2: Gaining Awareness Through Tracking and Reflection
Now that we understand money is really just another form of our life energy, let's take the next step—getting really clear about where that energy’s actually going.
How do you do that? Well, by tracking every dollar you earn and spend. It’s like holding up a mirror to your daily choices, and seeing your true financial habits and patterns—sometimes for the very first time.
I get it. Most people shy away from digging into their finances. Maybe you’re worried about what you’ll discover, or you assume it’s going to be a total drag. But here’s the thing: this isn’t about judging yourself. It’s about getting curious, a bit like keeping a food diary—not to shame yourself, but to notice what’s really going on, and make smarter decisions.
Even tracking your spending for just one month can be a real eye-opener. Those little habits—the morning coffees, the streaming subscriptions, that quick online buy you hardly remember—can pile up fast. When you jot down each transaction, you don’t just see the totals. You start to notice where your money naturally flows.
And hey, you don’t need a fancy system. A simple notebook, a spreadsheet, or a budgeting app will do the trick. The real secret is consistency. Make it a habit to note every expense, no matter how small. Over time, this log becomes like a mirror, showing you what really matters to you, and where your priorities might need a little nudge.
But don’t stop there. Try reflecting on the emotions behind your spending. Ask yourself—was this purchase triggered by boredom, stress, or did I truly need it? Did it bring real, lasting satisfaction, or was that pleasure gone in a flash? These questions help you see the motivations behind your choices, adding a deeper layer to simple numbers.
Here’s a practical way to put all this into action:
First, track every bit of income and every expense, and sort them into categories that make sense to you.
Next, revisit your real hourly wage—update that calculation if you need to.
Then, for each purchase, ask yourself: how many hours of my life did this actually cost?
And finally, after each transaction, pause to reflect—did this spending bring me joy or value, or was it just a quick fix?
As you stick with this, you’ll start to notice patterns. Maybe eating out eats up a surprising chunk of your budget, but rarely brings lasting happiness. Or you might find that a hobby, even if it’s a bit pricey, actually adds real meaning and joy to your life. These aren’t rules—they’re invitations. You get to decide what’s worth your energy.
Over time, this practice of tracking and reflection becomes second nature. You’ll feel more in control, more aware, and way more intentional with your choices. Instead of wondering where your money went, you’ll know exactly how your life energy is being spent. And that kind of awareness is the first big step toward transforming not just your finances, but your entire approach to living.
